title: Terrain Conqueror (v5)
description: A physics-based terrain trucking game with heavy, stable suspension, smooth engine torque, and satisfying grip — conquer rugged terrain, collect coins, and upgrade your rig.
prompt:
The game is a truck based game where the truck moves left to right to go over obstacles to gather money, however there are some issues with gravity, and suspension etc.

The truck physics need to be improved. Right now the vehicle feels light, slow, and bouncy, like it is made of rubber. I want the truck to feel heavy, stable and fun to drive, similar to games like Hill Climb Racing or Earn to Die.

The biggest issue is that the wheels appear to be attached directly to the body. Instead, every wheel should have a simple spring and damper suspension.

Each wheel should:

Compress upwards when hitting bumps.
Push the body back up with a spring force.
Use damping to absorb the impact and stop bouncing.
Return smoothly to its normal position after a bump.
Never continue bouncing more than once or twice after landing.

Reduce the vehicle's bounce by setting the wheel and body restitution (bounciness) close to zero.

Increase the body mass so the truck feels heavier than the wheels. The wheels should move to absorb bumps, not launch the entire truck into the air.

The engine should accelerate the truck using torque instead of instantly forcing the wheels to a speed. The truck should accelerate smoothly and feel responsive, but it should also have a noticeably higher top speed than it currently does.

Improve traction so the wheels grip the terrain instead of slipping or bouncing over every obstacle. Small rocks and bumps should compress the suspension instead of throwing the truck into the air.

When the truck lands after a jump, the suspension should absorb most of the impact. The body should settle quickly instead of bouncing repeatedly.

Please implement these changes by improving the existing physics system rather than replacing it. Keep the code clean, well commented, and make the suspension values (spring strength, damping, suspension travel, engine torque, mass, and grip) easy to adjust so they can be tuned later.

The end result should be a vehicle that feels heavy, smooth, stable, fast, and enjoyable to drive, rather than slow, rigid, and overly bouncy.
